HomePage.heroEyebrow: We check matching tools. We don’t replace them.
HomePage.heroTitleLead: Choosing a matching vendor? See which one gets your records right —
HomePage.heroBody: PairSight doesn’t match your records: it checks the tools that do. Bring each vendor’s results, and Jev, an independent AI checker, looks at the same pairs on its own, so you can see which vendor makes fewer wrong merges, which misses fewer duplicates, and why.
HomePage.howTitle: From vendor results to a clear choice, in three steps
HomePage.howBody: You bring your records and what each vendor matched in them. Jev checks the pairs without seeing what any vendor decided, and PairSight shows you where each vendor agrees with it and where it doesn’t.
HomePage.look1Body: Open a pair to see both records side by side, what differs, Jev’s score and what each vendor said.
HomePage.look2Body: Every run keeps exactly what it used: the values Jev saw, the match cut-off, Jev’s version and the vendors.
HomePage.look3Body: Choose how sure Jev must be before you see any results, so the numbers can’t be nudged afterwards.
HomePage.step1Body: Your records, plus the matches each vendor found in them, whether it lists pairs or groups. The vendors do the matching; PairSight checks it.
HomePage.step2Title: PairSight picks the pairs to check
HomePage.step2Body: It learns from your records which pairs are most likely to be the same, and adds every pair a vendor matched. You say what counts as the same, and how sure Jev must be.
HomePage.step3Body: Jev checks every pair without seeing what any vendor decided. PairSight lines its answers up against each vendor’s, side by side.
HomePage.limitsBody: PairSight helps you compare vendors and find their mistakes. It isn’t a matching tool, it doesn’t change your data, and its results aren’t a certificate of accuracy.
HomePage.limit1Title: Agreement with an AI, not proof
HomePage.limit1Body: Vendors are compared with Jev’s answers, and Jev can be wrong. Open any pair and use your own judgement.
HomePage.limit2Title: Only the pairs that get checked
HomePage.limit2Body: Pairs PairSight didn’t suggest and no vendor matched aren’t checked, so any duplicates among them stay unseen.
HomePage.limit3Body: One vendor may merge more carefully while another finds more duplicates. You decide which matters more.
HomePage.ctaBody: Start with your records and one vendor’s results. Or look around the demo first: no account needed.
HomePage.footer: Pairs are checked by Jev, TypeSafe’s AI. PairSight compares vendors; it doesn’t certify accuracy.

HomePage.who1Body: Running a trial with two or three matching vendors, and needing evidence rather than a sales demo.
HomePage.who2Body: Comparing vendors on the same records, with numbers you can explain to whoever signs off.
HomePage.who3Body: Giving a client an independent second opinion on a vendor’s matches.
HomePage.limit4Body: Your records stay in your account, and only you can see them. Jev sees only the values you choose to share: never record IDs, vendor names or what any vendor decided. Delete an evaluation and its records go with it.
HomePage.faq1Answer: No. Your vendors do the matching. PairSight checks their results against Jev’s answers on the same pairs, and shows you where they agree and where they don’t.
HomePage.faq2Answer: Jev is TypeSafe’s AI. It looks at each pair and says how sure it is that the two records are the same. It never sees what a vendor decided, so its answer is independent.
HomePage.faq3Answer: No. Its answers are a reference point, not proof. Every number leads back to pairs you can open and judge for yourself.
HomePage.faq4Question: What do I need to start?
HomePage.faq4Answer: Your records as a CSV or Excel file, at least {min, number, compact} of them, and at least one vendor’s results, as a list of pairs or a list of groups. The demo needs no account.
HomePage.faq5Question: How long does a check take?
HomePage.faq5Answer: It depends on how many pairs need checking. Before anything starts, the Plan shows how many pairs Jev will check and roughly how long it’ll take.

Report.title: Which vendor matched best?
Report.subtitle: {evaluation} · Run {number}
Report.verdict: On these {records, number, compact} records, {vendor} scored highest overall ({f1}), with the best balance of correct merges and duplicates found.
Report.verdictSingle: On these {records, number, compact} records, {vendor} agreed with Jev with an overall score of {f1}: Jev agreed with {precision} of its merges, and it found {recall} of the duplicates Jev found.
Report.verdictNone: No vendor could be scored yet: no checked pair was merged by a vendor or called the same by Jev. See what was checked on the last page.
Report.safest: Fewest wrong merges: {vendor}. Jev says only {share} of its merges are different records.
Report.mostComplete: Fewest missed duplicates: {vendor}. It found {share} of the pairs Jev says are the same.
Report.leadsEverywhere: {vendor} leads at every match cut-off from {from} to {to}, so this result doesn’t depend on where the cut-off was set.
Report.incompleteBanner: {count, plural, one {{count, number, compact} pair hasn’t} other {{count, number, compact} pairs haven’t}} been checked yet and {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} left out of every number. They may change once Jev checks them.
Report.precisionMeaning: Correct merges (also called precision): of the vendor’s merges, the share Jev says are the same. Low means wrong merges: two different customers, companies or products fused into one record.
Report.recallMeaning: Duplicates found (also called recall): of the pairs Jev says are the same, the share the vendor merged. Low means missed duplicates: one customer, company or product left as several records.
Report.f1Meaning: Overall score (also called F1): one number balancing the two, used to rank the vendors. It isn’t a measure of overall accuracy.
Report.caveat: Agreement with Jev, an AI · checked pairs only · not verified accuracy · no human review
Report.errorsIntro: The two ways a matching tool goes wrong, counted against what Jev says about the same pairs.
Report.mergesCount: {count, plural, =0 {No wrong merges.} one {{count, number, compact} wrong merge: a pair it merged that Jev says is different.} other {{count, number, compact} wrong merges: pairs it merged that Jev says are different.}}
Report.missesCount: {count, plural, =0 {No missed duplicates.} one {{count, number, compact} missed duplicate: a pair Jev says is the same that it didn’t merge.} other {{count, number, compact} missed duplicates: pairs Jev says are the same that it didn’t merge.}}
Report.patternSharedDiffer: These usually share {shared} but differ on {different}.
Report.sensitivityTitle: Does the ranking hold at other cut-offs?
Report.sensitivityIntro: Each vendor’s overall score (0 at the bottom, 1 at the top) if the match cut-off had been set anywhere from {from} to {to}. Where the lines don’t cross, the ranking doesn’t depend on the cut-off.
Report.headToHeadIntro: Only the pairs where two vendors disagree: one merged the pair, the other didn’t. Jev’s answer decides which one it agrees with.
Report.headToHead: Where only one of {a} and {b} matched a pair, Jev sided with {winner} in {wins, number, compact} of {total, number, compact}.
Report.headToHeadTie: Where only one of {a} and {b} matched a pair, Jev sided with each in {wins, number, compact} of {total, number, compact}.
Report.headToHeadNone: {a} and {b} merged exactly the same checked pairs.
Report.examplesIntro: The clearest disagreements for each vendor: the wrong merges and the missed duplicates Jev was surest about. Every pair is in this run’s CSV or Excel download.
Report.addedByVendor: a vendor’s match (PairSight didn’t suggest it)
Report.vendorLine: {file} · {format, select, pair {a list of pairs} other {a list of groups}} · {pairs, number, compact} merged pairs · confirmed complete {date}
Report.rulesIntro: Every pair PairSight suggested from the records, plus every pair a vendor merged.
Report.coverageLine: {total, number, compact} pairs checked: {suggested, number, compact} suggested by PairSight, {addedByVendor, number, compact} added because a vendor merged them.
Report.coverageStatus: {assessed, number, compact} checked · {failed, number, compact} couldn’t be checked · {pending, number, compact} not checked yet
Report.notCompared: The other {count, number, compact} possible pairs were never checked. If duplicates hide among them, nothing in this report can see them, so “duplicates found” only counts pairs that were checked.
Report.notComparedSuggested: PairSight suggested pairs that share something it compares: {type, select, company {a company number, tax ID, website, email, phone, postcode or a similar name} product {a barcode, part number, SKU, model or a similar name} other {a name, date of birth, email, phone or postcode}}. Pairs that share none of these weren’t checked, and nothing here can see duplicates among them.
Report.reused: {reused, number, compact} reused from earlier runs · {fresh, number, compact} checked in this run
Report.humanReview: None. Every answer here is Jev’s.
Report.glossaryBoth: Both say same: the vendor merged the pair and Jev says it’s the same.
Report.glossaryMerge: Wrong merge (only the vendor says same): the vendor merged the pair; Jev says it’s different.
Report.glossaryMiss: Missed duplicate (only Jev says same): Jev says the pair is the same; the vendor didn’t merge it.
Report.glossaryNeither: Both say different: the vendor and Jev agree these are different.
Report.glossaryAi: Jev is TypeSafe’s AI, used here as the yardstick. It can be wrong, so every number in this report measures agreement with Jev, not proven accuracy.
Report.verdictClose: On these {records, number, compact} records, {vendor} scored highest overall ({f1}), but only just: {runnerUp} scored {runnerUpF1}. Too close to choose on this score alone: the strengths below tell them apart.

Rules.title: What should Jev compare?
Rules.description: Tell Jev what counts as the same, what it gets to see, and how sure it needs to be. PairSight works out which pairs to check from your records.
Rules.thresholdDescription: Jev gives every pair a score from 0 to 1: how sure it is the two records are the same. Pairs at or above this cut-off count as a match. It doesn’t change Jev’s scores, only where the line is drawn, and you choose it before seeing any results so they can’t sway you.
Rules.thresholdNote_lenient: Close calls count as matches: catches more likely duplicates, but also more pairs that aren’t really the same.
Rules.thresholdNote_balanced: The starting point, well clear of where both kinds of score fall in our tests, so few pairs sit anywhere near it.
Rules.thresholdNote_strict: Only pairs Jev is confident about count: fewer wrong matches, but more duplicates left unmatched.
Rules.thresholdNote_custom: Pairs Jev scores {value} or more count as a match.

Welcome.title: Welcome to PairSight
Welcome.description: One thing before you start: what should we call you?
Welcome.nameHint: Shown on your account. You can use any name you like.

Overview.precisionTip: Of the pairs {vendor} merged, the share Jev also says are the same. Low means wrong merges. Also called precision.
Overview.recallTip: Of the pairs Jev says are the same, the share {vendor} also merged. Low means missed duplicates. Also called recall.
Overview.f1Tip: One number that balances correct merges and duplicates found, used to rank vendors. It isn’t overall accuracy. Also called F1.
Overview.coverageHowRules: PairSight suggested <n>{suggested, number, compact}</n> pairs worth checking. Every pair any vendor matched was added too: <n>{added, number, compact}</n> of those weren’t suggested.
Overview.coverageHowBlindSpot: Pairs PairSight didn’t suggest and no vendor matched weren’t checked, so a duplicate every vendor missed among them won’t show up here.
Overview.coverageBarLabel: {assessed, number, compact} checked, {pending, number, compact} not checked yet, {failed, number, compact} couldn’t be checked

coverage.addedByVendor: Added because a vendor matched it

Overview.coverageSuggested: PairSight suggested pairs that share something it compares: {type, select, company {a company number, tax ID, website, email, phone, postcode or a similar name} product {a barcode, part number, SKU, model or a similar name} other {a name, date of birth, email, phone or postcode}}. Pairs that share none of these weren’t checked, and nothing here can see duplicates among them.
Overview.coverageFootnote: Duplicates among pairs nobody picked can’t be seen. “Duplicates found” only counts pairs that were checked.
Overview.categoriesLabelFor: Pairs by who says what for {vendor}
Overview.agreedShare: {agreed, number, compact} of {total, number, compact} pairs

Overview.whyDescription: What the pairs they disagree on have in common

Overview.sensitivityDescription: How {vendor}’s numbers move as the match cut-off changes · from the scores Jev already gave

Overview.sensitivityMatches: <n>{count, number, compact}</n> pairs Jev says are the same
Overview.sensitiveAround: Any change to the cut-off moves these numbers
Overview.patternMissed: Pairs only Jev says are the same usually share {shared}: likely the same records written differently, which {vendor} didn’t merge.
Overview.patternMissedDiffer: Pairs only Jev says are the same usually share {shared} but differ on {different}: likely the same records written differently, which {vendor} didn’t merge.
Overview.patternMerged: Pairs only {vendor} merged mostly share {shared}: check for different records that happen to share contact details, addresses or names.
Overview.patternMergedDiffer: Pairs only {vendor} merged mostly share {shared} while {different} differ: check for different records that happen to share contact details, addresses or names.
Overview.topDescription: Where Jev and the vendor disagree most strongly
Overview.topMissedHint: Only Jev says same · Jev’s surest first
Overview.topMergesHint: Only vendor says same · Jev’s lowest scores first
Overview.workloadDisagreementsDetail: {pairsight, number, compact} only Jev says same · {vendor, number, compact} only the vendor says same
Overview.workloadNearDetail: Scores within {band} of the cut-off: a small change would flip these
Overview.workloadIncompleteDetail: Check them again from Detailed analysis
Overview.agreedTip: Pairs where {vendor} and Jev both say same, or both say different. “Both say different” is often the biggest group, so this isn’t what ranks the vendors: the overall score is.
